item.title: An Autumn Week of HomeGrown Development
item.description:
Wishlist HomeGrown on Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1894560/HomeGrown/
Play my previous game "Equilinox": https://store.steampowered.com/app/853550/Equilinox/
Support the channel on Patreon and get access to the game & code for Homegrown, the city-builder, and Equilinox: https://www.patreon.com/thinmatrix
Follow the game's progress on my social media: Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/thinmatrix/ Twitter: https://twitter.com/ThinMatrix Bluesky: https://bsky.app/profile/thinmatrix.bsky.social Trello: https://trello.com/b/W3zkIJTM/farm Email: thinmatrix@gmail.com
Background music by Jamal Green: https://open.spotify.com/artist/50jTMgIPZrjKFgHbCvoeRt?si=Z-xfUXEXQCuGdGRy7qf9Ug&dl_branch=1
Reasons for the fertilizer changes:
For most upgrades in the game, you purchase them once and then have the buff forever. Fertilizers are different because they degrade with the compost, so if you want to keep a buff on a given vegetable bed you need to keep purchasing more fertilizer and topping up. It’s like a subscription cost.
This means that if your fertilizer upkeep cost/minute for a soil tile is higher than the profit/minute that you’re making on that tile, then you could actually be making a loss. Problem is, it's quite hard to tell if that's the case without doing a careful cost/profit calculations for all your compost mixes and all your different crops to determine which vegetable beds are gaining or losing money, and that’s too much to ask a player to do in a casual game.
When playtesting, I would often be reluctant to even use fertilizers, because I just couldn't tell if they were helping, or losing me a load of money.
You could put time and money into setting up a high-tier compost mix which you use to provide benefits to all your vegetable beds, only for it to be quietly draining your profits if you use it with the wrong crops. That seemed rather harsh to me, and out of character with how all other upgrades in the game work.
I’m hoping that the new system will go some way towards fixing this. By making the player buy fertilizers in large amounts I can reduce the unit cost of the fertilizers to the point where it's almost irrelevant, while maintaining a reasonable barrier to entry with the increased initial cost (so you can’t buy them too early, and you still have to save up to get the good buffs). It's now harder to accidentally be losing loads of money without realizing it, and as a nice bonus you don’t have to buy new fertilizers as often.
The exact prices and amounts still need to be properly balanced. I also have some other variations of this idea that I could try if this doesn't work, but I want to give this idea a shot and playtest it for a bit first.
